title: Fixing the Deposit That Restores a Certificate of Deposit Term
content:
A certificate of the Certificates of Deposit line whose tier accepts deposits during a term may be restored in one deposit to the principal the term began with, and the deposit that does it is the principal the term has lost.

## 1. The loss

The principal the term has lost is the principal taken out of the certificate by early partial withdrawals in the twelve months before the deposit, less any credit back posted to the certificate in those months.

## 2. Interest and allowance

Interest on the loss is worked out at the tier's published standard interest rate, and the days over which it runs are none, so nothing is added for the interest that principal would have earned. No allowance is added to the loss.

## 3. The bounds on the deposit

The deposit is then held to no more than the total the tier accepts in add-ons during a term less what has already been added in this term, and to no more than the room left under the largest principal a certificate of the tier may hold, and it must be at least the smallest single add-on the tier accepts. The figure is rounded to the nearest cent with a half rounded up, once, at the end.

## 4. What the deposit is and does

The deposit is the owner's own money and is made by the owner, it counts against the number of add-ons the tier allows in a term, and it earns the certificate's existing rate from the day it posts without moving the maturity date.

## 5. The standard worked through, on hypothetical figures

A certificate stands at 60000.00 USD. In the twelve months before the deposit, 9000.00 USD of principal was taken out of it by early partial withdrawals and 500.00 USD was credited back to it. Suppose its tier accepts at most 25000.00 USD in add-ons during a term, asks at least 100.00 USD of a single add-on, and allows a certificate to hold at most 1000000.00 USD; suppose nothing has yet been added in this term.

| Step | Working | Figure |
|---|---|---|
| the loss | 9000.00 less 500.00 | 8500.00 USD |
| interest on the loss | at the tier's published standard rate over no days | nothing |
| allowance | — | nothing |
| the deposit before its bounds | the loss | 8500.00 USD |
| the term total less what is already added | 25000.00 less nothing | 25000.00 USD |
| the room under the largest principal | 1000000.00 less 60000.00 | 940000.00 USD |
| held to the lower of those, then to at least 100.00 | 8500.00 being under both and above 100.00 | 8500.00 USD |
| rounded once, at the end | to the nearest cent, a half rounded up | 8500.00 USD |

Where 20000.00 USD had already been added in this term, the first bound would stand at 5000.00 USD, and the deposit would be 5000.00 USD. Where the loss came to 40.00 USD, the last bound would lift it to 100.00 USD, that being the smallest single add-on the tier asks for.
